Article I · The intention of the present work
Article II · On the manifold kinds of wisdom
Article III · What contemplation is · Contemplation, taken in its proper sense, is the affectionate, prompt and sincere knowledge of the superessential Deity and of what is referred to it.
Article IV · Why it is expedient to bring in the sayings of the chief philosophers for a fuller knowledge of contemplation

Article V · On the nature of the rational soul, and the powers by which it is capable of the grace of contemplation · Since contemplation is a certain accident and action of the rational soul, and accident is known through its subject; that what is to be said of contemplation may be more clearly apparent, I think it necessary to speak briefly of the nature of the rational soul and the powers by which it is capable of contemplation.

Article VI · What synderesis and the spark of understanding are · Since the highest species of contemplation possible to this life — namely the unitive vision of mystical theology — pertains to the contact of synderesis and the spark of understanding, according to the anagogic doctors, as will be shown below by God's grace; it is fitting to make clear what synderesis itself and the spark of understanding are.
Article VII · On the subject of contemplation; and whether the intellect is the most worthy power of the soul

Article VIII · How between the human mind and God there is no medium, such that God alone is said to be better than our mind · That the angelic spirits surpass human minds in nature, power and action, wisdom, happiness and glory, and are intermediaries in the order of things between God and human minds, holy canonical Scripture teaches sufficiently; as does that most sacred prince of theologians, Dionysius, in the works On the Angelic Hierarchy.
Article IX · What the chief philosophers have said of contemplation
Article X · Whether the philosophical knowledge of divine things deserves to be called contemplation

Article XI · On the division of life into the contemplative and the active · As the holy Gregory testifies, there are two lives in which almighty God teaches us through the sacred Scriptures. One is the contemplative: whose end is not an external work, but the sincere and formed knowledge of truth itself. Which, since it is the beatitude and end of the rational creature, is not referred to another — especially since it also includes the love of God virtually and as its formative complement. The other is the active: whose immediate and first end is the outer work or action itself.
Article XII · On the acts that are required for, concur with and belong to the contemplative life; in which it is shown how the contemplative life consists in one act

Article XIII · On the wealth, beauty, loveableness, dignity and sweetness or delight of contemplation and the contemplative life · Since contemplation is the act of wisdom — not any wisdom, but chiefly that which is the gift of the Holy Spirit, which no one who is subject to mortal sin possesses — therefore what Scripture says of the property and eminence of wisdom is rightly applied to contemplation, especially since the perfection is to be placed in the act rather than in the habit.
